title: Field telemetry slim runbook for cost-aware day-2 operations
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This runbook describes a compact, operator-focused approach for telemetry collection and cost-aware observability on Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. It is intended for field operators, SREs, and solutions engineers who need a small, auditable telemetry footprint that preserves SLO visibility while minimizing egress, storage cost, and customer privacy scope.

Scope
- Applies to: Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packaged installations) instrumented with the Redwood agent (rwd-agent) and log/metrics collectors (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Fluent Bit).
- Not in scope: Hosted API telemetry, internal-only debug traces, or customer-specific legal evidence bundles (see related pages).

Goals
1. Provide deterministic SLO signal for tenant latency and error-rate with <= 5% sampling of request traces on steady state.
2. Limit telemetry egress to < 5 GB/day per 1000 qps baseline (configurable per-customer).
3. Maintain ability to perform safe canary upgrades and rollbacks with evidence for rollback decisions.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Reliability (oncall-field@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre / Telemetry Platform (telemetry@redwood.ai)
- Support escalation: customer-success (cs-ops@redwood.ai)

Key SLOs and thresholds
- Tenant request P95 latency: <= 250ms (in-cluster inference path)
- Token generation error rate: <= 0.5% (5xx or generation error)
- KV cache hit ratio (operational metric): >= 85% for steady-state batch-driven workloads
- Telemetry data budget: < 5 GB/day per 1000 qps baseline (default)
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Latency P95 > 300ms for > 5 minutes -> Sev2
  - Error rate > 1% for > 3 minutes -> Sev2
  - Telemetry egress spike > 200% of daily baseline -> Follow cost-exposure playbook

Telemetry sampling policy (slim default)
1. Metrics: 100% of critical metrics (latency histograms, error counters, KV cache metrics, GPU utilization) are emitted at 10s aggregation windows.
2. Traces: Adaptive head-based sampling at 5% baseline across tenants. During canary or incident investigations the sampling rate may be increased up to 100% for affected tenant-id(s) for a bounded window (default 15 minutes) via operator command.
3. Logs: Error logs (>= WARNING) are forwarded 100%. INFO/DEBUG logs are sampled at 1% by default and retained locally for 72 hours before pruning.
4. Model outputs or prompt payloads: never shipped out-of-band by default. Structured hashes and token-count metadata only. Full prompt text capture requires explicit customer consent and a separate evidence bundle workflow.

Cost-aware knobs (operator controls)
- rwd-agent config (example keys):
  - telemetry.metrics_window_seconds: 10
  - telemetry.trace_sampling.default_rate: 0.05
  - telemetry.trace_sampling.override_labels: ["canary","investigation"]
  - telemetry.log_retention_days: 3
  - telemetry.max_daily_egress_bytes: 5368709120

Small table: recommended defaults
| Setting | Default | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| metrics_window_seconds | 10 | Granularity for P95 computation without excessive cardinality |
| trace_sampling.default_rate | 0.05 | Preserves SLO signal while limiting trace volume |
| log_retention_days | 3 | Short retention reduces storage and privacy exposure |
| max_daily_egress_bytes | 5GB | Default cost guardrail; override for enterprise SLAs |

Runbook: common field scenarios
1) Scenario: sudden P95 latency regression (tiered detection)
   - Indicators: P95 > 300ms; KV hit ratio dropped > 10p; GPU utilization normal or high.
   - Immediate steps:
     1. Open incident channel and note tenant-id(s).
     2. Increase trace sampling to 50% for the tenant: rwd-agentctl set-sampling --tenant <TID> --rate 0.5 --ttl 15m
     3. Toggle prefix cache warmup: rwd-agentctl cache-warmup --tenant <TID> --prefix N=100
     4. If KV hit ratio remains low after 5 minutes, trigger safe-degrader to temporarily reduce batching: rwd-agentctl set-batching --max_batch_tokens 256
     5. If latency remains > 350ms for 10m, follow capacity-failover (see Appendix).
   - Owner: oncall-field; Escalate to eng-serving-runtime after 15 minutes if no improvement.

2) Scenario: telemetry egress spike / cost exposure
   - Indicators: telemetry egress > 200% of daily baseline, or billing alert for customer overage.
   - Immediate steps:
     1. Throttle debug-level logs: rwd-agentctl set-log-sample --level INFO --rate 0.01
     2. Reduce trace sampling to 1% globally: rwd-agentctl set-global-sampling --rate 0.01
     3. Enforce egress cap (soft): rwd-agentctl set-egress-cap --bytes <customer-budget> --action drop_noncritical
     4. Notify CS and provide suggested customer-facing message template (appendix).
   - Owner: telemetry@redwood.ai; notify billing@redwood.ai for potential credits or contract changes.

3) Scenario: model swap or quantization fallback fails post-upgrade
   - Indicators: generation errors spike, model load failures, increased 5xx.
   - Immediate steps:
     1. Activate rollback marker for model switch: rwd-controller mark-rollback --model <model-id> --reason "failed-sanity"
     2. Roll back to previous model binary via operator command: rwd-controller model-activate --model <previous-version> --force --wait 120s
     3. Re-run post-deploy smoke tests (script below) and validate token-generation correctness and latency within thresholds.
   - Owner: field-operators + runtime-team; open postmortem if > 30 minutes.

Upgrade & rollback procedures (compact)
- Pre-upgrade checklist (operator must verify):
  1. Backup operational snapshot: rwd-agentctl snapshot --type runtime-state --dest /var/backups/rwd-<date>.tgz
  2. Confirm customer acceptance window and maintenance window.
  3. Ensure telemetry sampling is elevation-ready (operator can increase sampling).
  4. Verify resource headroom: GPU idle > 15% or autoscale budget available.
  5. Confirm canary tenant(s) selected and smoke tests prepared.

- Canary upgrade steps:
  1. Deploy to canary tenant(s) with 5–10% of traffic.
  2. Monitor: P95 latency, error-rate, KV cache ratio, telemetry anomaly score for 10 minutes.
  3. If metrics stable, incrementally increase traffic in 3 steps (25%, 50%, 100%) with 10–15 minute observation windows.
  4. If any step fails, abort and execute rollback.

- Rollback steps (fast path):
  1. Mark rollback in control plane for audit: rwd-controller annotate --key rollback --value "operator-fast-rollback"
  2. Revert model/service image to previous tag: rwd-controller service-revert --service <svc> --tag <previous> --parallelism 4
  3. Force telemetry sampling to high for affected tenants to collect forensic data: rwd-agentctl set-sampling --tenant <TID> --rate 1.0 --ttl 30m
  4. Validate via smoke tests and keep rollback evidence bundle (see Customer evidence section).

On-prem packaging & field constraints (concise)
- Package characteristics: signed images, minimal sidecar footprint, no outbound plaintext prompts by default.
- Recommended runtime sizing (minimal field profile):
  - 2 x 48GB GPU nodes (for smaller footprints) or 4 x 80GB nodes for model fanout;
  - 64GB RAM per node; 2 x 1Gbps uplink (or 10Gbps dataplane for high throughput);
  - Disk: 1TB NVMe local for model cache and ephemeral state.
- Firmware and supply chain: ensure TPM attestation and image signature verification prior to activation.

Customer acceptance evidence (what to collect)
1. Compact evidence bundle for rollback validation:
   - operational snapshot (runtime-state tgz),
   - metrics window CSV (10m pre and post),
   - sampled traces (restricted to hashes and metadata unless consent obtained),
   - smoke-test results and logs (errors only).
2. Document the change in customer-facing template and record via ticketing system with timestamped artifacts.

Appendix A: CLI snippets and smoke test
- Increase sampling for tenant:
  rwd-agentctl set-sampling --tenant tenant-42 --rate 0.5 --ttl 15m
- Snapshot runtime state:
  rwd-agentctl snapshot --type runtime-state --dest /var/backups/rwd-$(date +%F).tgz
- Revert service image (fast path):
  rwd-controller service-revert --service inference-svc --tag v2026-02-01 --parallelism 4

Smoke test (bash)
#!/bin/bash
set -e
# quick smoke: 10 requests spread across model variants
for i in {1..10}; do
  curl -s -X POST \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{"model":"gpt-mini-redwood","input":"hello world"}' \
    http://localhost:8080/v1/generate | jq '.latency_ms, .status'
  sleep 1
done

Notes and limitations
- This runbook provides a compact operator workflow intended to reduce customer exposure and telemetry costs. It intentionally omits full forensic capture (which is handled by the evidence preservation playbook). For high-risk regulated customers, follow the restricted evidence and compliance runbooks in the related pages.
